qs.q: Which specific broad-spectrum antibiotic used for prolonged neutropenia is noted to have an elevated rate of associated Clostridium difficile diarrhea?
qs.e: Imipenem/cilastatin has been specifically associated with an elevated rate of C. difficile diarrhea among the standard anti-pseudomonal beta-lactam options. Ceftazidime and cefepime share equal efficacy profiles without this specific highlighted association.

qs.q: Which specific antibiotic commonly used for prolonged neutropenia has been associated with an elevated rate of Clostridium difficile diarrhea?
qs.e: Imipenem/cilastatin has been specifically associated with an elevated rate of C. difficile diarrhea among the standard antipseudomonal regimens. Other regimens like ceftazidime do not share this specific association in the text.

qs.q: Superinfections, such as Clostridium difficile-associated diarrhea, are more common with broad-spectrum antibiotics that disrupt the normal gut flora.
qs.e: Superinfections occur when antibiotics kill off beneficial bacteria in the body, allowing opportunistic pathogens like Clostridium difficile or Candida to overgrow. Broad-spectrum antibiotics affect a wider range of bacteria, including those in the normal flora, thus increasing the risk of superinfections.

qs.q: Superinfections, such as Clostridium difficile-associated diarrhea or candidiasis, are more common with which type of antimicrobial therapy?
qs.e: Broad-spectrum antibiotics disrupt a wider range of normal microbiota, allowing for overgrowth of resistant organisms or opportunistic pathogens, leading to superinfections.
